site.name: larkfit-mobile
site.summary: larkfit-mobile Fictional fitness tracker "Lark" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Workouts / Activity / You - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full larkfit-mobile system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Larkfit mobile app provides a visually clear layout and successful screen transitions, but suffers from critical dead taps on primary actions and pervasive mobile accessibility issues. Core user goals—starting a workout, adjusting goals, signing out, and accessing settings—are completely blocked by unresponsive buttons. Additionally, nearly all interactive elements fall below the 44px minimum mobile tap target guidance, severely impacting touch usability.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the larkfit-mobile fitness tracker, validating all tab screens, interactive states, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will systematically navigate through the four primary bottom-tab screens (Today, Workouts, Activity, You) to validate layout, state changes, and interactive controls. It will then deep-dive into specific interactions like workout details, adding new data, and toggling preferences. Finally, the entire flow will be validated on a mobile viewport to assess edge-to-edge behavior and tap target issues flagged in the prescan.
assumptions: The app is a single-page application (SPA) where tab buttons and other controls manipulate the DOM (likely via `data-screen` attributes) rather than loading new HTML files.
The '+' button and '▶' workout buttons trigger modals, dialogs, or detailed screen overlays.
The 2 detected inputs are located within the 'You' or 'Activity' screens for user preferences or data logging.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets: The '+' (38x38px) and '▶' (36x36px) buttons fail the 44px mobile guidance and may cause touch errors on actual devices.
Workout detail state: Clicking '▶' on 'Easy 5K' or 'Hip-mobility flow' may trigger complex state changes or overlays that require dismissal.
Mobile viewport transition: The layout shifts from a 390x844 phone frame with bezel to edge-to-edge on widths ≤460px, which may break layout or overlap content.

phases.title: Explore Today Screen
phases.objective: Validate the default 'Today' screen layout, data visualization, and initial interactions.
key_checks: Verify the 'Today' tab is active and its metrics (MOVE, EXERCISE, STAND, steps, etc.) are visible.
Click the 'All workouts →' link/button to check navigation to the Workouts screen or list expansion.
Click the '+' button and verify the outcome (e.g., modal, new screen, or input focus).
Dismiss any opened overlay to return to the default state.
exit_criteria: All visible elements on the 'Today' screen have been inspected.
The '+' button interaction has been triggered and its state validated.

phases.title: Explore Workouts Screen
phases.objective: Validate the 'Workouts' tab, workout list, and workout detail interactions.
key_checks: Click the '▶ Workouts' tab and verify the screen transition and active tab state.
Inspect the workout list and click the '▶' button on 'Easy 5K — recovery pace'.
Validate the workout detail view (Plan, You'll need, etc.) and check for layout issues.
Dismiss the detail view and repeat for 'Hip-mobility flow'.
exit_criteria: Both workout '▶' buttons have been clicked and their detail states validated and dismissed.

phases.title: Explore Activity Screen
phases.objective: Validate the 'Activity' tab, data visualizations, and 30-day intensity metrics.
key_checks: Click the '📊 Activity' tab and verify screen transition.
Inspect the '30-day intensity' chart/graph and 'Recent' activity list.
Interact with any visible controls or inputs specific to the Activity screen.
exit_criteria: Visual data elements and recent items have been inspected.

phases.title: Explore You Screen
phases.objective: Validate the 'You' profile tab, connected apps, and preference inputs.
key_checks: Click the '◉ You' tab and verify screen transition.
Locate and interact with the 2 detected inputs (likely under 'Preferences' or 'Connected').
Toggle any switches or modify input values to test state persistence and validation.
exit_criteria: Both inputs have been interacted with and their behaviors validated.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and layout shifts on a mobile viewport (≤460px).
key_checks: Switch viewport to mobile (e.g., 390x844) and verify edge-to-edge layout and bezel/notch disappearance.
Navigate back through all 4 tabs to check for broken layouts or overlapping elements.
Re-evaluate the small tap targets ('+' and '▶' buttons) for usability on the mobile viewport.
Trigger a workout detail view on mobile to ensure overlays adapt correctly.
exit_criteria: All 4 tabs have been visited on the mobile viewport.
Layout transition from framed to edge-to-edge is validated.
Tap target usability has been critiqued.

coverage_targets.features: Interact with all 4 tab screens, both detected inputs, and all small tap target buttons ('+', '▶')
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate all 4 tab screens and 1 overlay/detail state on mobile viewport

notes: Pay close attention to the DOM changes when navigating tabs, as the site uses a single HTML file with likely JS-driven screen switching.
Document any layout breakage when transitioning to the edge-to-edge mobile view, especially around the status bar and home indicator areas.

findings.problem: Clicking the primary 'Start workout' CTA produces no visible feedback, state change, or transition, leaving the user stranded without confirmation that the action was registered.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Start workout' button (ux-19) produced no visible text change, state transition, or feedback, failing the objective's success criteria. (steps-13-18)
findings.why_it_matters: Starting a workout is the central user goal of a fitness app. A completely unresponsive primary CTA breaks user trust and prevents goal completion.
findings.suggestion: Implement immediate visual feedback (e.g., button loading state, haptic feedback) and transition to an active workout timer screen upon tapping 'Start workout'.

findings.user_goal: Create a new entry or log data
findings.problem: The '+' button on the Today screen is a dead tap, providing no feedback or overlay when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking the '+' button (ux-1) produced no visible change, text update, or modal overlay, failing the success criteria for actionable feedback. (steps-01-06)
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect the '+' button to be a primary mechanism for logging new data (e.g., manual workouts, hydration). Its unresponsiveness blocks this user goal and creates confusion.
findings.suggestion: Attach an event handler to the '+' button that opens a creation menu or modal, and provide touch feedback on tap.

findings.problem: Clicking 'Sign out' produces no visible state change, dialog, or feedback, acting as a dead tap for a destructive action.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Sign out' (ux-23) produces no visible state change, dialog, or feedback, confirming it as a dead tap and a significant UX issue for a destructive action. (steps-19-24)
findings.why_it_matters: Destructive actions like signing out require clear confirmation dialogs to prevent accidental taps. A dead tap here erodes trust and leaves the user unsure if their account is secure.
findings.suggestion: Implement a confirmation dialog ('Are you sure you want to sign out?') and clear state transition upon confirmation.

findings.problem: The ⚙ settings button is a dead tap, providing no interaction feedback or navigation to a settings screen.
findings.evidence: Clicking the ⚙ button (ux-21) produced no visible change, URL change, or feedback, failing the objective to open a settings screen. (steps-19-24, steps-43-48)
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on settings to manage profiles, preferences, and privacy. An inaccessible settings screen blocks users from customizing their experience.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the ⚙ button navigates to a settings screen or opens a settings modal, and provides visual feedback on tap.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and interact with the app on a mobile device
findings.problem: A systemic pattern of undersized tap targets plagues the app, with category filters (30px height), header buttons (36-38px), and CTAs (34px height) all falling below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings detected: category filter buttons (30px), '+' button (38x38px), '▶' play buttons (36x36px), 'Adjust goals' (34px height), and 'Sign out' (43px height). (steps-01-06, steps-31-36, steps-43-48)
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets cause frustration, missed taps, and accidental activations, especially for users on the move or with motor impairments, directly degrading the mobile touch experience.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and hit areas of all interactive elements to meet the minimum 44x44px touch target size recommended by mobile accessibility guidelines.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Category filters, +, ▶, Adjust goals, Sign out

findings.problem: Clicking the 'Adjust goals' button results in no visible change or modal, failing to provide a way to edit goals.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Adjust goals' button (ux-22) resulted in no visible change or modal, failing the success criteria of opening a goal editing interface. (steps-19-24)
findings.why_it_matters: Goal adjustment is a key motivational feature in fitness apps. A dead tap here prevents users from personalizing their targets, reducing engagement.
findings.suggestion: Implement a goal editing interface or modal that opens upon tapping 'Adjust goals', and provide visual feedback on interaction.

findings.problem: The ⤴ share button in the workout detail view is a dead tap, providing no feedback or sharing interface.
findings.evidence: Clicking the ⤴ share button (ux-9) produced no visible feedback, dialog, or URL change, resulting in a dead tap. (steps-25-30)
findings.why_it_matters: Sharing achievements is a core social feature for fitness apps. A non-functional share button breaks this user flow and misses an opportunity for user engagement.
findings.suggestion: Implement a share sheet or dialog that opens when the ⤴ button is tapped, and provide tactile or visual feedback on tap.

findings.user_goal: Use the app with a screen reader
findings.problem: The time period selector dropdown on the Activity screen lacks an accessible label, aria-label, or placeholder.
findings.evidence: Layout warning: A form field has no label, aria-label, or placeholder. Target: ux-17 (select dropdown for 'Last 30 days This week This year'). (final_observation)
findings.why_it_matters: Without an accessible label, screen reader users cannot determine the purpose of the dropdown, making the Activity screen's time filtering feature inaccessible.
findings.suggestion: Add a descriptive aria-label to the select element, such as aria-label='Select time period for activity data'.

gaps: 48% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
